title: Polynomial sample complexity for deletion-trace reconstruction
decision_reason: Explicit primary question and independent scholarly corroboration; current general bound and apparent resolutions compared in full relevant scope. A33 and local math, link, layout and catalogue checks passed. One accepted family; not yet an active catalogue entry.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Unknown binary string x; independent traces from deleting each bit independently with known probability q.
problem_fingerprint.domain: x ranges over all {0,1}^n; each observed trace has length at most n and retains order.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: No distribution, sparsity, separation, codebook, or nearby-reference promise on x.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Known n and fixed q; deleted positions not observed.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Every fixed q in (0,1), then all integers n≥2.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every q there exist finite Cq,kq and, for each n, one decoder succeeding on every x from at most ceil(Cq n^kq) traces.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: One sample is one complete independently deleted copy; success probability ≥2/3.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Exact recovery of every bit; worst-case over x, probability over deletions and decoder randomization.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: q fixed independently of n; constants may depend on q.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Information-theoretic decoder, no running-time or statistical-query restriction.

statement_source_and_scope_match: ALN25 explicitly asks polynomial sufficiency at constant deletion rate. SB21 §V independently repeats it; BPRS20 §IV defines worst-case trace complexity, and BVW26 Definition 2 supplies the 2/3 convention. Constant error probabilities above 1/2 are equivalent up to constant repetition factors.
proposed_statement_text: For every fixed q∈(0,1), can a decoder recover every unknown n-bit binary string with probability at least 2/3 from at most Cq n^kq independent deletion traces, with no time restriction?
applied_significance: Foundational sample budget for reconstructing a molecularly stored sequence from repeated reads with missing symbols; ignores insertions, substitutions and clustering.
